description: The publisher-manifest validity cases of tzun-anchor/1 §9 and §13: a manifest entry for the real publisher whose validFrom or validUntil sits at, just inside or just outside the time of the block that holds the publication, the leap days the format allows and the leap second it refuses, and the verdict of tzun-anchor/1 §10.4 for each, presented three ways. Both ends of a window are inclusive and compared at full precision: a block time is a whole second, so a validFrom with any non-zero fraction admits only a block at a later second, and a validUntil with one still admits a block at its own second. Then the transaction cases of §10.4 item 2: signed transactions at each edge of the rules item 2 states (Chain id: a typed transaction on chain id 0; Legacy v: a v of 35 or 36, or any other below 37 but 27 and 28; Signature values: r outside [1, n - 1], s outside [1, n/2] or a typed yParity other than 0 or 1; Fees: an EIP-1559 tip above its fee cap; Recovery: a signature from which no public key recovers; Encoding: a rawTransaction that is not the canonical RLP of its fields; Field sizes: a nonce or gasLimit above 2^64 - 1, a chain id, value, gasPrice or fee above 2^256 - 1, or a legacy v above 2 * (2^256 - 1) + 36), each with the transaction just inside the edge where there is one, and the verdict of §10.4 for each, offline. Ethereum mainnet, Sepolia and Hoodi, the chains of the network table of §9, refuse a transaction that breaks one of these rules under the rules they apply today, so no block they produce today holds one. A development chain can be more lenient: anvil, for one, mines a transaction whose s is above n/2. A refused transaction is false, malformed_publication, on any chain, whatever an Ethereum library would recover from it. The header-source cases §13 also lists for this file are not in it.
source: Generated by scripts/generate-evm-anchor-vectors.ts, which reads each bound by its own transcription of §9 (full precision, the fraction kept as digits) and states each verdict from §10.4, calling no SDK code. The publication, its block and the publisher are epoch 0 of anchor-e2e-vectors.json, byte for byte: signed and mined on anvil, and checked there by the Go gate with go-ethereum. The transaction cases are signed by the script with the throwaway key of the EIP-155 example (0x46 repeated, RFC 6979 signatures), or carry a signature built to recover a chosen way, and the script reads each against its own transcription of §10.4 item 2. scripts/regenerate-vectors.ts --anvil rewrites this file right after anchor-e2e-vectors.json.

format.publication: The evm-calldata/1 publication with its heavy material, as anchor-e2e-vectors.json epochs[0].publication; p is its P, sender the address its signature recovers to, blockTime the unix seconds of its block (headerSource.blocks[0].timestamp).
format.headerSource: The header source the header and noHeader modes use: its chain id, its finality, its finalized height, the canonical block at each height it lists (none at any other), and the transactions it looks up by transactionId (none other).
format.manifestEntry: The entry every case starts from, for anchorOrigin: the publisher on the file's chain. A case's bounds are set on it, and its manifest is { "publishers": { anchorOrigin: [ entry ] } }.
format.validityBounds: name; bounds, the members set on manifestEntry (an absent member is left absent, null is set to null); window, whether §9 makes the entry valid at blockTime (admits, excludes) or unreadable (malformed); expect, per mode, the verdict of verifyEvmPublication: valid, reason (absent when valid is true), the anchor.evm.tx and anchor.evm.canonical checks, each with outcome and reason (absent when checked-correct), and inclusion when valid is true.
format.modes: header: the publication as given (blockHeader, txIndex and txProof carried), with headerSource, so the window is judged at the header's time (§10.4 item 6) and again at the time the source confirms (item 13). noHeader: the publication without blockHeader, txIndex and txProof, with headerSource, so the window is judged only at the time the source confirms, and the source's lookup places the transaction (item 12). offline: the publication as given and no header source, so the header can make the publication fail but never pass.
format.transactionCases: chain, blockNumber and blockHash: what every case's publication claims (no header, no trie proof, no header source: offline). A case is { "kind": "evm-calldata/1", "chain": chain, "transactionId": transactionId, "rawTransaction": rawTransaction, "blockNumber": blockNumber, "blockHash": blockHash }, verified for P = p of this file and anchorOrigin, with the manifest { "publishers": { anchorOrigin: [ { "address": publisher, "chain": chain, "namespace": "test" } ] } }. Each case: id; name; rule, the rule of item 2 it breaks, by the specification's label (chain-id: Chain id, legacy-v: Legacy v, signature-values: Signature values, fees: Fees, recovery: Recovery, encoding: Encoding, field-sizes: Field sizes), or null when item 2 reads it; each refused case breaks that rule and no other; item2, refuses or reads; rawTransaction and transactionId (its keccak-256); publisher, the address the signing key has, or for a signature no key made, the address it recovers (for a high s, read as n - s with the other parity); sender, the address item 2 recovers (null when it refuses); expect, the verdict of verifyEvmPublication, as for validityBounds. An encoding or field-sizes case is the signing key's signature over the canonical encoding of the same field values, so a reader that took the values would recover the publisher.
